newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical says to sue Circon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical says to sue Circon.

text.p: United States Surgical Corp said on Tuesday it filed a suit against Circon Corp, asking a Delaware court to prohibit and void Circon's recently adopted "poison pill" and "golden parachutes."

The lawsuit claimed Circon's board of directors breached fiduciary duties by taking these steps for the "improper sole purpose of cementing Circon President and Chief Executive Officer Richard Auhll's continuing control over the company," U.S. Surgical said in a statement.
U.S. Surgical made an $18 per share unsolicited bid for Circon Corp and Circon has strongly recommended that its shareholders do not tender their shares.
Circon declined to comment until it had been served notice of the lawsuit.

"The lawsuit cites Mr. Auhll's recent statement to Circon's employees that Circon has 'retained expert financial and legal advisors to help us prevail, no matter what USS does' as confirmation that Circon's board has determined to resist any offer threatening Mr. Auhll's control, regardless of the price of the offer or the consquences of such resistance to Circon's shareholders," U.S. Surgical said.
The lawsuit also said Circon's stated desire to protect benefits of last year's purchase of Cabot Medical Corp did not justify the "poison pill," the company said.
U.S. Surgical said it would continue to pursue a merger with with Circon.

"We are committed to pursuing a combination of U.S. Surgical and and Circon," a U.S. Surgical spokesman said in a statement. "Our cash tender offer of $18 per share resulted in nearly seven million shares being tendered as of August 29, 1996 despite the efforts Circon's management undertook to discourage shareholders from tendering."

The company also said it would shortly file a separate lawsuit in Delaware Chancery Court seeking to compel Circon to provide it with full information needed to let U.S. Surgical communicate directly with Circon shareholders about the offer.
"USS has requested this information from Circon pursuant to its rights under Delaware law, but to date Circon has refused to provide all such information," it said.
U.S. Surgical said as a result of Circon's "poison pill" rights plan, its offer was now conditioned upon the redemption of these rights.
